title: Concurrency vs Parallelism: The Core Idea

scenes.line1: Are threads always running at once?
scenes.say: Are threads always running at the same time? Let's clear up the real difference between concurrency and parallelism.
Concurrency means multiple tasks are making progress, but not necessarily at the same instant. Parallelism is when tasks actually run at the same time, usually on different CPU cores.

scenes.label: Threads
scenes.say: Threads share memory within a process. They let you do work concurrently, but you have to manage access to shared data.
If two threads access shared data without a lock, you risk a race condition. Protect the critical section with a lock to keep things safe.

scenes.question: Does concurrency always mean parallelism?
scenes.right: No. Concurrency means progress, not simultaneous execution.
scenes.say: Interview trap: concurrency does not always mean parallelism. Concurrency is about making progress, not necessarily running at the same time.
